summary: Adds --ui-bg-accent-subtle-hover, the accent wash under the pointer. The Table sheet drew a selected+hovered row as a raw hex (#C3DBE7) and annotated it 'new token', and neither existing role could stand in: bg-hover is a neutral and would drop the selection colour on hover, while bg-accent would make one hovered row louder than the button that submits the page. Derived as withAlpha(accent, 0.20) — the same step --ui-intent-danger-bg-hover takes over its own tint — and pinned in ZERO_AUTHORED in BOTH schemes, to the sheet's hex in light and to the matching alpha in dark. Also lists ten contrast pairs a table row is the first thing to render: secondary and muted ink on the accent wash, on bg-hover and on bg-active; the focus ring on bg-surface rather than on the page; and secondary ink on the sunken well. Declaring them moved one shipped token toward more contrast: dark's --ui-text-secondary steps lighter, raising every dark secondary-ink pair in the library (6.97 to 7.91 on the page, 9.13 to 10.36 on a control). Deliberately NOT listed is --ui-bg-accent-legible against those washes. It was, briefly, for a 3px selection edge the sheet annotates and never paints — and flooring the token against the wash as well as the sunken well darkened it from #518CA2 to #458096, deepening the Switch track, the Slider fill and thumb ring, the Progress fill and ImageUpload's, none of which are tables. The edge is not shipped, so the pair is not declared: an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair, but a pair nothing renders is a constraint on every component that does. The four browser tests that failed while the token moved were each named 'uses the ROLE, not the palette step' and each asserted a hard-coded rgb() copy of what the role resolved to the day it was written; they now read the role, which is the fix that outlives this.

migration.manual: A resolver that enumerates BRANDABLE_TOKENS gains one entry and will fail to type-check until it derives it — that is intended. Re-emit your theme CSS (`pnpm tokens` in the storybook app, or your own emitter) or `bg-accent-subtle-hover` compiles to nothing. One existing token moves: dark's secondary ink lightens. Nothing in light changes. If you have pinned a token's value in a test, read the token instead.
